**Tour dates:** 5–12 February

## Trip highlights

Carnival opens the trip. You’ll spend several days in Rio, with evening events, free time and private tours.

At Copacabana Palace, you’ll stay in a Deluxe Ocean View Room with breakfast. The hotel is also home to the Michelin-starred Cipriani restaurant, which serves Italian food and has a wine list and live piano music.

Ride the eco train through the Tijuca Forest up Corcovado. Afterwards, a private guide will show you the historic centre, including the Arcos da Lapa, the Selarón Steps, the Municipal Theatre and the Metropolitan Cathedral.

On the night of 6 February, the Carnival Ball takes place at Copacabana Palace. It starts at 22:00 and continues until dawn.

The next day includes a 30-minute helicopter flight over Rio and the Champions Parade at the Sambadrome. The programme includes a private six-person Frisa box in Sector 4, in the A/B front row.

After Carnival, travel to Iguazú Falls and stay in a Junior Suite with breakfast at Belmond das Cataratas. The hotel is inside the national park, so you can visit the falls during quieter hours before the park opens to the public or after it closes.

The Brazilian side offers panoramic views of the cascades, and a private Macuco Safari boat takes you close to the rushing water. On the Argentine side, take the eco train and follow walkways over the river to the Devil’s Throat.

## What makes this a luxury tour

The premium experience starts with how the trip is organised. You’ll be met at the airport, take private transfers between stops, tour with English-speaking guides and travel by deluxe minivan on land.

At the Sambadrome, you’ll watch the parade from a Frisa box in Sector 4. The six A/B front-row seats offer a good view of the parade. Your transfer with a guide is private, so you can leave before the programme ends if you’d like.

The Carnival Ball at Copacabana Palace offers a different way to celebrate. The overnight event takes place in the hotel’s grand function rooms, with evening wear, Carnival costumes, music and fine dining. The ball starts at 22:00 and continues until dawn.

There’s downtime between the busy evenings. The mornings after the ball and the Sambadrome are both free, and the whole fifth day is yours to spend as you like. Sleep in, linger over breakfast, head to the ocean, visit the Botanical Garden or Parque Lage, or explore Ipanema’s shops, galleries and cafés.

The helicopter flight offers another perspective. It takes about 30 minutes and passes over the lagoon, Leblon, Ipanema, Copacabana, Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain. It’s one of the trip’s main events between the Carnival Ball and the Champions Parade.

In Iguazú, the location of Belmond das Cataratas inside the national park allows you to visit the falls before most visitors enter the park or after they leave. The itinerary also includes a private Macuco Safari boat trip.

The itinerary leaves room to rest between major evening events. There are free hours or a full day at leisure after the ball, the Sambadrome and active excursions.

## VIP programme

The tour includes English-speaking guides on excursions and transfers, private transfers and transport by deluxe minivan.

The Carnival programme includes parade tickets and a private transfer with an English-speaking guide.

You can leave the Sambadrome early if you wish. A private transfer is provided.

Meals at certain restaurants and some optional activities are at your own expense unless they’re specifically listed as included.

VIP Access / Fast Track to Sugarloaf Mountain on day 4 is included. Another Fast Track service costs extra. The type of service is unspecified, so please confirm the details when booking.

## Accommodation

Spend five nights at Belmond Copacabana Palace in Rio.

Room category: Deluxe Ocean View Room.

Spend two nights at Belmond das Cataratas in Iguazú.

Room category: Junior Suite.

Breakfast is included at both hotels.
